key_concepts: Earth's interior heat is a source of geothermal energy
Conventional geothermal systems use steam from geysers or high-pressure depths
Supercritical geothermal systems use magma-heated water circulating through permeable rock
Geothermal power plants use deep Earth heat to produce steam and generate electricity
Geothermal heat pumps use shallow Earth heat for heating water or buildings
